title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 3 — Angles
question: Angle types, then the angle facts: straight line, around a point, crossing lines, triangles, parallel lines.
intro:
**Ten cards, one idea each.**

- Look at the figure.
- Tap **Show working** for the example.
- Type your answer and press **Check**.

**Key facts:**

\[\begin{aligned} \text{straight line} &= 180^\circ \\ \text{around a point} &= 360^\circ \\ \text{triangle} &= 180^\circ \end{aligned}\]

questions.title: Types of angles
questions.prompt:
- **acute**: less than \(90^\circ\)
- **right**: exactly \(90^\circ\)
- **obtuse**: between \(90^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\)
- **straight**: exactly \(180^\circ\)
- **reflex**: between \(180^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\)
questions.figure_alt: Five angles side by side: acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex.
steps:
**Example:** an angle of \(128^\circ\).

It is more than \(90^\circ\) and less than \(180^\circ\).

\[128^\circ \to \boxed{\text{obtuse}}\]

practice.intro: A reflex angle is less than one full turn.
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: Angles on a straight line
questions.prompt:
- Angles on a straight line **add up to \(180^\circ\)**.
- Missing angle = \(180^\circ\) − the angle you know.
questions.figure_alt: A straight line with one ray; the left angle is 130 degrees and the right angle is x.
steps:
**Example:** \(130^\circ\) and \(x\) on a straight line.

\[\begin{aligned} x &= 180^\circ - 130^\circ \\ &= \boxed{50^\circ} \end{aligned}\]

practice.intro: Two angles on a straight line: \(72^\circ\) and \(x\).
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: Angles around a point
questions.prompt:
- Angles all the way **around a point add up to \(360^\circ\)**: one full turn.
- Add the angles you know, then take the total from \(360^\circ\).
questions.figure_alt: Three rays from one point make angles of 150 degrees, 120 degrees and x.

practice.intro: Two angles around a point: \(200^\circ\) and \(x\).
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: Vertically opposite angles
questions.prompt:
- Two straight lines cross: **opposite angles are equal**.
- Neighbouring angles sit on a straight line, so they **add up to \(180^\circ\)**.
questions.figure_alt: Two crossing lines: an angle of 40 degrees, x opposite it, and y next to it.

practice.intro:
- Two lines cross.
- One angle is \(115^\circ\).
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: Angles in a triangle
questions.prompt:
- The three angles of any triangle **add up to \(180^\circ\)**.
- Add the two you know, take the total from \(180^\circ\).
questions.figure_alt: A triangle with angles 50 degrees and 60 degrees at the base and x at the top.

questions.title: Isosceles triangles
questions.prompt:
- **Isosceles**: two equal sides (the tick marks).
- The two **base angles** next to the third side are **equal**.
questions.figure_alt: An isosceles triangle with ticks on its two equal sides; the top angle is 40 degrees and both base angles are x.
steps:
**Example:** the top angle is \(40^\circ\).

\[\begin{aligned} x + x &= 180^\circ - 40^\circ \\ 2x &= 140^\circ \\ x &= \boxed{70^\circ} \end{aligned}\]

practice.intro: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of \(100^\circ\).
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: The exterior angle
questions.prompt:
- Make one side of a triangle longer: the angle outside is the **exterior angle**.
- Exterior angle = the **two opposite inside angles added**.
questions.figure_alt: A triangle with inside angles 50 and 60 degrees; the base is extended on the right and the outside angle is y.
steps:
**Example:** the inside angles opposite are \(50^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\).

\[\begin{aligned} y &= 50^\circ + 60^\circ \\ &= \boxed{110^\circ} \end{aligned}\]

practice.intro: The two opposite inside angles are \(45^\circ\) and \(75^\circ\).
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: Corresponding angles (F)
questions.prompt:
- The arrows mark **parallel** lines.
- Angles in the **same position** at each crossing are **equal**: an **F** shape.
questions.figure_alt: Two parallel lines cut by a slanted line; 65 degrees at the top crossing and x in the same position at the bottom.
steps:
**Example:** the top angle is \(65^\circ\).

Same position at the bottom crossing:

\[x = \boxed{65^\circ}\]

practice.intro:
- A corresponding angle is \(70^\circ\).
- Find its neighbour on the straight line.
head: Question
Answer

questions.title: Alternate angles (Z)
questions.prompt:
- Between the parallel lines, on **opposite sides** of the slanted line.
- Alternate angles are **equal**: a **Z** shape.
questions.figure_alt: Two parallel lines and a slanted line; 48 degrees below the top line on the left and x above the bottom line on the right.

questions.title: Co-interior angles (C)
questions.prompt:
- Between the parallel lines, on the **same side** of the slanted line.
- Co-interior angles **add up to \(180^\circ\)**: a **C** shape.
questions.figure_alt: Two parallel lines and a slanted line; on the left side between the lines, 110 degrees at the bottom and x at the top.
